concept.title: Uniqueness of the Critical 2-Vertex Augmentation of G27
concept.concept_description: The paper demonstrates that augmenting the 27-vertex unit-distance graph G27 with a specific pair of vertices results in a 29-vertex graph with geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4. The authors note that such augmentations are exceedingly rare. This conjecture posits that, up to Euclidean isometry, this specific 2-vertex augmentation is the unique way to add two vertices to G27 such that the resulting unit-distance graph has a geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4.
concept.mathematical_framing: The paper demonstrates that augmenting the 27-vertex unit-distance graph G27 with a specific pair of vertices results in a 29-vertex graph with geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4. The authors note that such augmentations are exceedingly rare. This conjecture posits that, up to Euclidean isometry, this specific 2-vertex augmentation is the unique way to add two vertices to G27 such that the resulting unit-distance graph has a geometric fractional chromatic number strictly greater than 4.
concept.lean_guess: Formalize the 27-vertex graph G27 and the convex polytope of its 23 extremal geometric fractional colorings. Then, perform a verified exhaustive search or algebraic classification over all possible 2-vertex additions, verifying that only the specific pair identified in the paper yields a unit-distance graph where the geometric fractional chromatic number exceeds 4.

concept.title: Generalized scalar factor for mixed modified Greaves‑Jing‑Zhu operators
concept.concept_description: We conjecture that for any deformation parameters t and s the mixed product of the modified Greaves‑Jing‑Zhu operators yields a scalar factor that can be expressed as a rational function of infinite q‑Pochhammer symbols: F(t,s;u) = (u;t)_\u221e (‑u;s)_\u221e / ((‑u;t)_\u221e (u;s)_\u221e). Moreover, the q‑expansion of F(t,s;u) has palindromic coefficients and satisfies a finite‑order linear recurrence; after removing the alternating signs the coefficients are non‑negative integers.
concept.mathematical_framing: We conjecture that for any deformation parameters t and s the mixed product of the modified Greaves‑Jing‑Zhu operators yields a scalar factor that can be expressed as a rational function of infinite q‑Pochhammer symbols: F(t,s;u) = (u;t)_\u221e (‑u;s)_\u221e / ((‑u;t)_\u221e (u;s)_\u221e). Moreover, the q‑expansion of F(t,s;u) has palindromic coefficients and satisfies a finite‑order linear recurrence; after removing the alternating signs the coefficients are non‑negative integers.
concept.lean_guess: The conjecture can be approached by first expressing the mixed product via the diagonal conjugation that relates the modified operator to the classical neutral operator. Using known product formulas for neutral operators and Bailey‑pair theory, one can reduce the mixed product to a ratio of infinite q‑Pochhammer symbols as stated. The resulting rational function is then analyzed via standard q‑series techniques (e.g., the pentagonal number theorem) to extract its q‑expansion, prove palindromicity and derive a finite‑order recurrence. The non‑negativity of the sign‑adjusted coefficients follows from known positivity results for principal specializations of one‑row Schur Q‑functions and can be formalized using Lean’s algebraic number theory libraries.
